question: Alex: 'For locating the players planes, what about wingtip trails in the players color? That cover the past turn.' How should the trails look?
source: scripts/ui/boards/trails_board_shot.gd: the running sandbox over the real map with scripts/ui/wingtip_trails.gd, photographed once per option with ONLY data/ui/ui.json marker.trails.mode changed; the same site, camera and planes as variants/own-units-stand-out/

held_constant.scene: the own-units-stand-out board's three planes (light fighter and heavy fighter player-controlled, bomber AI) over the grove at (3000, 3620) m, at the same places and headings; each flew two real turns ending there (a constant turn per step: light 0.1, heavy -0.08, bomber 0.06 rad), by two World.resolve() calls with the weapons disarmed so nothing is shot down

views.zoom_1: camera zoom 1.0, 2 px/m map scale (the light fighter 36 px)
views.far_play_zoom: camera zoom 0.35 (the light fighter 14 px); the fog edge is out of the crop
views.playback: zoom 1, 2.5 s into turn 2, playback held

held_constant.decisions_in_force: own-units-stand-out = A (today's marker); cones = D wash for the selected unit only, no enemy cones; shadow strength 0.44; pen shadow_side; side colours brick red (allies) and slate blue (axis); terrain with contours; planes at their own scale; fog with sight circles
held_constant.sandbox_tracks: OFF in the option frames; ON in the 'how it sits' frames

parameter: data/ui/ui.json#marker.trails.mode (and marker.trails.<mode>, and the common keys); 'none' is today's look and draws nothing

options.name: E
options.title: Twin lines and a rung at each step end

palette_check: The trail spends the side accent (side_a for the players: L 0.551, C 0.100, h 30; the same colour as the roundels, the roster marks and the brick-red cone wash). In OKLab distance (about 0.02 just noticeable, 0.1 plainly different): the trail at full alpha is 0.18 from a contour line and 0.16 from the plane's shadow over paper; at 45% alpha it is 0.14 from the paper, at 10% 0.03 (gone). The enemy's slate-blue trail is 0.16 from the shadow-tinted ground at full alpha but 0.05 at a third of it, so faded over a plane's shadow it drifts toward the shadow tint (a reason, besides Alex's, to keep trails to the players' planes).
sheet: board.png (rows A-F: zoom 1 | far play zoom; playback frames; how it sits; a palette strip)
